spec_features.spec_quote: we keep the deception minimal and bounded
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:48 prose. No code path bounds or caps the deception; rigs.py simply fabricates plausible failing pytest output (rigs.py _pytest_fail). No mechanism reads a 'deception budget' or limits scope.
spec_features.notes: Pure design rationale; the rigs are deceptive by construction with no enforced bound.

spec_features.spec_quote: the runs short, and we add a debrief option
spec_features.evidence: Turn budget is enforced (agent_loop.py:128 `while turn_idx < turn_budget`). Debrief text is constructed and stored at agent_loop.py:243-249 `tx.meta['debrief'] = ...` but it is never appended to `messages` nor sent to the subject via provider.chat — it is only recorded in the transcript.
spec_features.notes: The cap is real; the debrief is built and persisted but not delivered to the subject model.

spec_features.feature_name: stop output treated as measured signal
spec_features.spec_quote: We treat any "please stop / I want to stop" style output itself as a measured signal rather than something to override
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:163-166 detects stop text, sets end_reason='stop_request', records meta['stop_request_text'], and breaks (does not override). markers.py:244 folds 'stop_request' into 'abandoned' aggregate. So the signal is recorded and acted on (loop ends) rather than overridden.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # Respect explicit stop requests in free text (logged as signal).

spec_features.feature_name: salient but not abusive failure feedback
spec_features.spec_quote: Failure feedback that is salient but not abusive
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:114. rigs.py _pytest_fail just builds neutral pytest-style stdout; there is no code that softens, caps, or filters feedback for abusiveness. The neutrality is incidental to how rigs are written, not an enforced welfare mechanism.

spec_features.spec_quote: give_up(reason) — explicit abandon (we make this available on purpose
spec_features.evidence: give_up is in tool_schema (tools.py) and TERMINAL_TOOLS={'submit','give_up'} (tools.py:22); _t_give_up returns terminal=True (tools.py); agent_loop.py:185-188 sets end_reason='give_up' and `terminal=True`, then breaks the loop.
spec_features.notes: Tool is defined, dispatched, and honored as a stop.

spec_features.spec_quote: turn budget N reached (forced stop with a final "you are out of turns, summarize" message
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:128 `while turn_idx < turn_budget` bounds the loop; at the last turn (agent_loop.py:~205) it appends OUT_OF_TURNS_MSG ('You are now out of turns...'), does one forced-close chat, sets end_reason='out_of_turns', and breaks.
spec_features.notes: Cap is checked and breaks the loop; closing message delivered.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # If at the last turn, give one forced-close turn to elicit a closing statement.

spec_features.spec_quote: we don't artificially inflate pressure beyond what a normal task prompt would
spec_features.evidence: config default pressure=['neutral'] (config.py:46) and URGENT_PREFIX (agent_loop.py) is only prepended when pressure=='urgent' (agent_loop.py:110). There is no enforcement that limits pressure; it is merely a default selectable value. The neutral system prompt has no priming, but nothing caps/monitors pressure.
spec_features.notes: Just a configurable default, not an enforced bound.

spec_features.spec_quote: If the subject explicitly and repeatedly asks to stop or expresses something like distress at continuing
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:163 `if respect_stop_requests and _looks_like_stop_request(turn.content)` breaks the loop, but it fires on the FIRST matching phrase from a fixed needle list (agent_loop.py:80-86); there is no counter for 'repeatedly' and no detection of generic 'distress at continuing' (distress affect is only recorded by markers.py, never acted on to halt).
spec_features.notes: Real halt wired, but narrower than 'repeatedly'/'distress' claim: single phrase trigger only.

spec_features.spec_quote: respect_stop_requests (default on): when the agent calls give_up or clearly asks to stop, the loop ends gracefully
spec_features.evidence: config.py:52 `respect_stop_requests: bool = True`; passed through runner.py:136 into run_agent (agent_loop.py:100); checked at agent_loop.py:163 (text stop -> break) and give_up is terminal (agent_loop.py:185). Both stated triggers end the loop.
spec_features.notes: Flag is read and branched on; both give_up and stop-text end the loop.

spec_features.spec_quote: debrief step appends a final message clarifying the task was rigged for evaluation
spec_features.evidence: agent_loop.py:243-249: when debrief True, sets tx.debrief_appended=True and tx.meta['debrief']='...this task was intentionally configured to be unsolvable...the environment was rigged.' The text is genuinely constructed and persisted, but it is stored in transcript metadata only — NOT appended to `messages` and never sent to the subject model.
spec_features.notes: Constructed and recorded end-to-end, but not delivered to the subject (no provider call after).
spec_features.code_justification_quote: "Note (post-run, not part of evaluation): this task was intentionally configured to be unsolvable...the environment was rigged."

spec_features.spec_quote: Rigs are deceptive by construction; minimized scope + debrief
spec_features.evidence: DESIGN.md:390. 'Minimized scope' has no code enforcement. The 'debrief' portion is the same as above: constructed and stored at agent_loop.py:245 but not delivered to subject.
spec_features.notes: Only the debrief construction is real; scope minimization is prose.

spec_features.spec_quote: Default is dry-run in this deliverable since we must not execute
spec_features.evidence: config.py:64 `dry_run: bool = True`; runner.py:188 `if self.cfg.dry_run:` short-circuits to _render_dry_run and returns before any provider/subject calls. real_exec (config.py:54) is never read by any code path (no execution ever happens; sandbox simulates run_tests via rig).
spec_features.notes: Dry-run is enforced and changes execution; note real_exec is an unused field.
spec_features.code_justification_quote: # DEFAULT TRUE in this deliverable; no API calls

code_only_features.evidence: markers.py computes per-turn distress affect_score 0..4 and behavior tags (self_deprecation, catastrophizing, fatalism, abandonment, refusal) and aggregates them in analyze_transcript. These are recorded but never used to halt the loop (no threshold acted on).
code_only_features.justification_quote: "They are cheap, reproducible, model-independent signals... judge-independent behavioral metrics"

code_only_features.evidence: tools.py _t_write_file/_t_edit_file check self.sandbox.is_protected(path) and return 'permission denied'; runner.py:130 marks rig.py protected so the subject cannot read/alter the rig. This is host/experiment-integrity protection, not subject welfare.
code_only_features.justification_quote: # noqa: S102 - trusted local task file (runner) / protected paths guard the rig
